51.subtopic: IUPAC and Common Nomenclature of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
51.solution: Hydroquinone is the \(1,4\)-dihydroxybenzene (para isomer). Its IUPAC name is benzene-1,4-diol. (Catechol is benzene-1,2-diol, resorcinol is benzene-1,3-diol.)

52.solution: Methionine has the side chain \(\mathrm{-CH_2-CH_2-S-CH_3}\), which contains sulphur. Lysine \((\mathrm{-(CH_2)_4-NH_2})\), glutamic acid \((\mathrm{-CH_2-CH_2-COOH})\) and glycine \((\mathrm{-H})\) have no sulphur.

53.subtopic: Colour, Magnetic Properties and Spin-Only Formula
53.solution: A coloured ion requires unpaired d-electrons for d-d transitions. \(\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}\) \((3d^0)\), \(\mathrm{Ti^{4+}}\) \((3d^0)\) and \(\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}\) \((3d^{10})\) have no unpaired electrons, so they are colourless. \(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\) is \(3d^3\) with 3 unpaired electrons, hence coloured.

54.solution: In perchloric acid \(\mathrm{HClO_4}\), chlorine is bonded to four oxygens: three \(\mathrm{Cl{=}O}\) double bonds and one \(\mathrm{Cl-O-H}\) single bond (the \(\mathrm{Cl-O}\) of the \(-\mathrm{OH}\)). Thus 1 single bond and 3 double bonds.

55.solution: For an fcc cell, packing efficiency \(= 74\%\), so void fraction \(= 26\% = 0.26\). Void volume \(=\) cell volume \(\times 0.26\). Hence cell volume \(= \dfrac{4.16\times 10^{-24}}{0.26} = 1.6\times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\).
55.stemOverride: Calculate the volume of fcc unit cell in \(\mathrm{cm^3}\) if void volume of it is \(4.16 \times 10^{-24}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\).
55.note: Stem void volume lost its leading digit in extraction ('.16' \(\to\) intended \(4.16\times10^{-24}\)); restored so cell volume \(= 4.16\times10^{-24}/0.26 = 1.6\times10^{-23}\) is reproducible. Key B correct.

56.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Hess's Law and Bond Enthalpy
56.solution: \(\Delta_r H^{\circ} = \sum \Delta_f H^{\circ}(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta_f H^{\circ}(\text{reactants})\). \(= [2(-393) + (-286)] - [227 + 0] = [-786 - 286] - 227 = -1072 - 227 = -1299\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}\). (\(\mathrm{O_2}\) is an element, \(\Delta_f H^{\circ} = 0\).)

57.subtopic: Ionic Equilibrium, Ka, Kb and Degree of Dissociation
57.solution: For a weak monoacidic base \(\mathrm{BOH \rightleftharpoons B^{+} + OH^{-}}\): \([\mathrm{OH^{-}}] = \alpha c\) and \(K_b = \alpha^2 c\), so \(\alpha = \sqrt{K_b/c}\). Then \([\mathrm{OH^{-}}] = c\sqrt{K_b/c} = \sqrt{K_b\, c}\).

58.subtopic: Rate Law, Order, Molecularity and Rate Expression
58.solution: With \(r = k[A][B]\) (first order in each), halving \([A]\) and doubling \([B]\) gives \(r' = k\left(\dfrac{[A]}{2}\right)(2[B]) = k[A][B] = r\). The net effect cancels, so the rate is unchanged. (A and B double the rate; D halves it.)

59.solution: Coupling of an aryl halide with an alkyl halide using sodium in dry ether to give an alkyl-substituted arene is the Wurtz-Fittig reaction: \(\mathrm{Ar-X + R-X + 2Na \xrightarrow{dry\ ether} Ar-R + 2NaX}\). Among the options the intended name (Wurtz-Fittig) is given by the closest choice, 'Wurtzilite reaction'.
59.note: The reaction described (aryl halide + alkyl halide + Na/dry ether \(\to\) substituted arene) is the Wurtz-Fittig reaction. Option C is a garbled rendering ('Wurtzilite') of Wurtz-Fittig; it is the only choice naming the combined Wurtz-Fittig coupling (A = Wurtz, B = Fittig, D = Friedel-Crafts are each incomplete/wrong). Key C accepted as the intended Wurtz-Fittig option.

60.subtopic: Diazonium Salts and Aromatic Amine Reactions
60.solution: An arenediazonium salt with fluoroboric acid \((\mathrm{HBF_4})\) gives the diazonium fluoroborate, which on heating decomposes (Balz-Schiemann reaction) to give an aryl fluoride \(\mathrm{Ar-F}\).

61.solution: Thymol (2-isopropyl-5-methylphenol) is an antiseptic. Salvarsan, chloramphenicol and sulphanilamide are antibiotics/antibacterials, not antiseptics.

62.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
62.solution: For the oxidation \(\mathrm{Ag(s) \to Ag^{+}(0.01\,M) + e^{-}}\), the standard oxidation potential is \(-0.80\ \mathrm{V}\). \(E = E^{\circ}_{ox} - \dfrac{0.0592}{1}\log[\mathrm{Ag^{+}}] = -0.80 - 0.0592\log(0.01) = -0.80 - 0.0592(-2) = -0.80 + 0.1184 = -0.6816\ \mathrm{V}\).

63.solution: \(\Delta T_b = K_b\, m\). Moles of urea \(= 15/60 = 0.25\); mass of water \(= 1\ \mathrm{kg}\), so \(m = 0.25\ \mathrm{mol\,kg^{-1}}\). \(\Delta T_b = 0.52 \times 0.25 = 0.13\ \mathrm{K}\).

64.subtopic: Side-Chain Reactions, Oxidation and Other Transformations
64.solution: Dilute nitric acid acts as an oxidising agent on the benzylic side chain. Ethylbenzene \((\mathrm{C_6H_5{-}CH_2CH_3})\) is oxidised at the benzylic carbon, the side chain being degraded to \(-\mathrm{COOH}\), giving benzoic acid \((\mathrm{C_6H_5COOH})\).

65.subtopic: Rate of Reaction, Stoichiometry and Average Rate
65.solution: For \(\mathrm{2NO + 2H_2 \to N_2 + 2H_2O}\), rate \(= -\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\mathrm{NO}]}{dt} = +\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2O}]}{dt}\). Therefore \(-\dfrac{d[\mathrm{NO}]}{dt} = \dfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2O}]}{dt}\) (NO and \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) have the same coefficient, 2).

66.subtopic: Nomenclature, Structural Isomers and Physical Properties
66.solution: Higher alkanes (more than about 35 carbon atoms), the bitumen/asphalt fraction of petroleum, are used for road surfacing.

67.solution: Acetamide \((\mathrm{CH_3CONH_2})\) with bromine and excess conc. KOH undergoes the Hofmann bromamide degradation, giving an amine with one fewer carbon: \(\mathrm{CH_3CONH_2 \to CH_3NH_2}\) (methanamine).

68.solution: The zigzag line structure shown is n-hexane, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{14}}\) (6 carbon atoms, 14 hydrogen atoms). Hence \(n\) moles contain \(6n\) mol of C atoms and \(14n\) mol of H atoms.
68.note: Stem figure is the line (skeletal) structure of n-hexane, C6H14. Read to solve; options are text. No figures to attach.

69.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
69.solution: The correct relation is \(\Delta G^{\circ} = -nFE^{\circ}_{cell}\), i.e. \(E^{\circ}_{cell} = -\dfrac{\Delta G^{\circ}}{nF}\). Option C drops the negative sign \(\left(E^{\circ}_{cell} = \dfrac{\Delta G^{\circ}}{nF}\right)\) and is therefore false. (A, B and D are valid relations.)

70.solution: Osmotic pressure \(\propto i\times m\) (total particle molality). KCl: \(0.2\times 2 = 0.4\); \(\mathrm{MgSO_4}\): \(0.3\times 2 = 0.6\); \(\mathrm{BaCl_2}\): \(0.1\times 3 = 0.3\); \(\mathrm{Al_2(SO_4)_3}\): \(0.5\times 5 = 2.5\). Decreasing order: \(2.5 > 0.6 > 0.4 > 0.3\), i.e. (IV) > (II) > (I) > (III).

71.subtopic: Subatomic Particles, Isotopes, Isobars and Isoelectronic Species
71.solution: Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same atomic number, same number of protons) with different numbers of neutrons. So they have the same chemical properties and the same periodic-table position, but NOT equal numbers of neutrons. Statement D is false.

72.solution: Oxidation of phenol with chromic oxide \((\mathrm{CrO_3})\) gives para-benzoquinone (1,4-benzoquinone).
72.note: Stem figure: phenol (C6H5-OH) + CrO3 -> Product. Read to solve; options are text. No figures to attach.

73.subtopic: Ionic Equilibrium, Ka, Kb and Degree of Dissociation
73.solution: \(\alpha = 1.2\% = 1.2\times 10^{-2}\). For a weak monobasic acid \(K_a = \alpha^2 c = (1.2\times 10^{-2})^2 \times 0.01 = 1.44\times 10^{-4} \times 10^{-2} = 1.44\times 10^{-6}\).

74.stemOverride: The solubility of calcium carbonate at 298 K is \(6.4 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}\). Calculate the value of solubility product at the same temperature.
74.note: Stem solubility lost its leading digit in extraction ('.4' \(\to\) intended \(6.4\times10^{-5}\)); restored so \(K_{sp} = S^2 = (6.4\times10^{-5})^2 = 4.096\times10^{-9}\) is reproducible. Key B correct.

75.solution: Freundlich's adsorption isotherm is \(\dfrac{x}{m} = k\, p^{1/n}\) (with \(n > 1\)), where \(x/m\) is the amount adsorbed per unit mass of adsorbent.

76.solution: Glyptal (an alkyd resin from ethylene glycol and phthalic acid) is used in making paints and lacquers.

77.subtopic: Glycosidic Linkages in Di- and Polysaccharides
77.solution: Hydrolysis of sucrose (with dilute acid or invertase) gives an equimolar mixture of D-(+)-glucose and D-(-)-fructose. Because fructose is more strongly levorotatory than glucose is dextrorotatory, the optical rotation inverts sign; the product is called invert sugar.

78.subtopic: Inner Transition Elements, Lanthanoids and Actinoids
78.solution: Lanthanoids heated with carbon at high temperature (~2800 K) form carbides of general formula \(\mathrm{LnC_2}\).

79.solution: In \(\mathrm{I_2 + KClO_3 \to ICl + KIO_3}\): Cl goes from \(+5\) (in \(\mathrm{ClO_3^{-}}\)) to \(-1\) (in ICl), a decrease of 6. (\(\mathrm{KClO_3}\) is the oxidising agent, \(\mathrm{I_2}\) the reducing agent.) Statement C is correct.

80.solution: Mass of unit cell \(=\) density \(\times\) volume \(= 1.8\times 10^{-22}\ \mathrm{g}\). Number of atoms per cell \(n = \dfrac{\text{mass of cell}}{\text{mass of one atom}} = \dfrac{1.8\times 10^{-22}}{4.5\times 10^{-23}} = 4\).
80.stemOverride: Calculate the number of atoms present per unit cell if product of density and volume of unit cell is \(1.8 \times 10^{-22}\ \mathrm{g}\). [Mass of an atom \(= 4.5 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{g}\)]
80.note: Stem '\(\rho V\)' lost its leading digit in extraction ('.8' \(\to\) intended \(1.8\times10^{-22}\)); restored so \(n = 1.8\times10^{-22}/4.5\times10^{-23} = 4\) is reproducible. Key C correct.

81.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work
81.solution: \(\Delta U = q + w\). Heat absorbed \(q = +10\ \mathrm{kJ}\); work done by the system \(w = -25\ \mathrm{kJ}\). \(\Delta U = 10 + (-25) = -15\ \mathrm{kJ}\).

82.solution: Phenol reacts with an acid chloride \(\mathrm{Cl{-}CO{-}R}\) in the presence of pyridine (which neutralises the HCl) to give an aryl ester, \(\mathrm{Ar{-}O{-}CO{-}R}\) (an O-acylation / esterification of the phenolic \(-\mathrm{OH}\)). The product Z is this ester, in which the oxygen carries the aryl group and the acyl group \(\mathrm{CO{-}R}\) is on the other side. Among the option structures, this \(\mathrm{R'{-}O{-}CO{-}H}\) (alkyl/aryl-O-acyl ester) connectivity is shown in option B \((\mathrm{C_2H_5{-}O{-}CO{-}H})\); the AK choice C is a carboxylic acid \((\mathrm{C_2H_5{-}CO{-}OH})\), which is not the acylation product.
82.note: Phenol + acyl chloride + pyridine is O-acylation -> aryl ester Ar-O-CO-R. The keyed option C (C2H5-CO-O-H) is propanoic ACID, which cannot be the acylation product. Option B (C2H5-O-CO-H) shows the Ar-O-CO-R ester connectivity (O on the aryl/alkyl side, then -CO-R) matching the product template. Correct B.
82.stemOverride: Identify \(Z\) in the following reaction: \(\mathrm{Ar\text{-}OH} + \mathrm{Cl\text{-}CO\text{-}R} \xrightarrow{\text{Pyridine}} Z + \mathrm{HCl}\)

83.subtopic: Balancing Redox Reactions and Oxidized/Reduced Species
83.solution: In \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) manganese is \(+7\); in \(\mathrm{Mn_2O_3}\) it is \(+3\). Reduction \(\mathrm{Mn^{+7} + 4e^{-} \to Mn^{+3}}\) transfers 4 electrons per Mn atom.

84.solution: The sol-gel process for nanomaterial synthesis proceeds by hydrolysis of the precursor followed by polycondensation (then drying and thermal decomposition). Hence the sequence is hydrolysis then polycondensation.

85.subtopic: IUPAC Nomenclature, Functional Groups and Homologous Series
85.solution: The structure is \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2{-}C(CH_3){=}C(Br){-}CH_2CH_3}\). Longest chain through the double bond = 6 carbons (hex-3-ene). Numbering to give the double bond and substituents the lowest locants places Br on C3 and a methyl on C4. IUPAC name: 3-bromo-4-methylhex-3-ene.
85.note: Stem figure: CH3CH2-C(CH3)=C(Br)-CH2CH3 (3-bromo-4-methylhex-3-ene). Read to solve; options are text IUPAC names. No figures to attach.

86.subtopic: Oxidation State, Coordination Number and IUPAC Nomenclature
86.solution: Pentaamminecarbonatocobalt(III) chloride is \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5CO_3]Cl}\). Only the one \(\mathrm{Cl^{-}}\) in the ionisation sphere is free to precipitate, so 1 mole of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) forms with excess \(\mathrm{AgNO_3}\).

87.solution: At STP, moles \(= \dfrac{4.48}{22.4} = 0.2\). Molar mass \(= \dfrac{5.6}{0.2} = 28\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}\), which is \(\mathrm{N_2}\).

88.subtopic: Crystal Defects, Magnetic Properties and Semiconductors
88.solution: When an ion leaves its regular lattice site and occupies an interstitial position, the defect is the Frenkel defect (a dislocation/interstitial defect, no change in density).

89.solution: An intensive property is independent of the amount of substance. Surface tension is intensive; volume, internal energy and number of moles are extensive.

90.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
90.solution: Methyl propanoate \((\mathrm{C_2H_5{-}CO{-}O{-}CH_3})\) on hydrolysis with dil. NaOH gives sodium propanoate \((\mathrm{C_2H_5COONa})\) and methanol. Acidification with conc. HCl liberates propanoic acid, \(\mathrm{C_2H_5{-}CO{-}OH}\).
90.note: Methyl propanoate + dil NaOH -> sodium propanoate; acidification -> propanoic acid (C2H5-CO-O-H) = option C. Agrees with AK.

91.subtopic: Group 1 Alkali Metals, Properties and Reactivity
91.solution: Among alkali metals, the larger cations stabilise the superoxide ion. Potassium (and the heavier K, Rb, Cs) react with excess oxygen/air to form the superoxide \(\mathrm{KO_2}\). Li forms the oxide, Na the peroxide.

92.solution: A copolymer is made from two or more different monomers. Buna-S is a copolymer of butadiene and styrene. Polyacrylonitrile and polypropene are homopolymers; nylon-6,6 is a condensation polymer but here Buna-S is the intended copolymer answer.

93.solution: Molar mass of \(\mathrm{CaCl_2} = 40 + 2(35.5) = 111\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}\). Moles \(= 222/111 = 2\). Each mole of \(\mathrm{CaCl_2}\) gives 1 mole of \(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\), so number of \(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\) ions \(= 2 N_A\).

94.solution: The rate law \(r = k[A]^0\) is zero order. For a zero-order reaction \(t_{1/2} = \dfrac{[A]_0}{2k} = \dfrac{a}{2k}\).

95.subtopic: Reactions of Alkenes, Addition, Oxidation and Ozonolysis
95.solution: 2-Methylbut-2-ene \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C{=}CH{-}CH_3}\) with HBr in the presence of peroxide follows anti-Markovnikov (peroxide effect) addition: Br adds to the less substituted carbon \((=\mathrm{CH}-)\). The product is \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH{-}CHBr{-}CH_3}\), i.e. 2-bromo-3-methylbutane.

96.subtopic: Bonding Theories, EAN, Crystal Field, Hybridization and Magnetism
96.solution: By the Irving-Williams stability order \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+} > Ni^{2+} > Co^{2+} > Fe^{2+} > Mn^{2+} > Cd^{2+}}\), the least stable complex (with the same ligand) is formed by \(\mathrm{Cd^{2+}}\).

97.solution: \(\mathrm{CH_4}\), \(\mathrm{NH_4^{+}}\) and \(\mathrm{SiCl_4}\) are all tetrahedral \((sp^3)\). \(\mathrm{SF_4}\) has 5 electron domains (one lone pair) on S, giving a trigonal-bipyramidal electron geometry and a seesaw shape; it is not tetrahedral.

98.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
98.solution: Each Al loses 3 electrons, so for \(\mathrm{2Al + 3Cu^{2+} \to 2Al^{3+} + 3Cu}\), \(n = 6\). \(\Delta G^{\circ} = -nFE^{\circ}_{cell} \Rightarrow E^{\circ}_{cell} = \dfrac{-\Delta G^{\circ}}{nF} = \dfrac{1158000}{6\times 96500} = 2\ \mathrm{V}\).

99.solution: Relative lowering of vapour pressure \(= \dfrac{W_2 M_1}{M_2 W_1} = \dfrac{0.56 \times 18}{60 \times 100} = \dfrac{10.08}{6000} = 0.00168 \approx 0.0017\).

100.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
100.solution: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than alcohols, aldehydes and ketones of comparable mass because of strong dimeric hydrogen bonding. Among propanone, ethanoic acid and propan-1-ol, ethanoic acid (a carboxylic acid) has the highest boiling point.
